guest.bio_context: Tom Heckman has spent over 20 years in manufacturing and automation. He started in the 1980s working for an Allen Bradley distributorship in their engineering department, focusing on data collection and manufacturing data aspects including PLCs. He later owned and operated an integration business for many years before founding Sepasoft in 2010. Recently, he transitioned from CEO to CTO to focus on the technology side of the business.

pending_qa.q: What challenges do manufacturers face when preparing MES data for artificial intelligence applications?
pending_qa.r: Many manufacturers struggle with getting clean MES data into AI systems. MES data isn't static after initial recording—quality results change, tests run after 24 hours, production counts get updated, and various corrections happen over time. The key challenge is correcting data that goes up to AI so that AI can learn from accurate data instead of bad data.

pending_qa.q: What new advanced analysis capabilities is Sepasoft introducing to simplify AI implementation in manufacturing?
pending_qa.r: Sepasoft is releasing a product combining connectors like MQTT, API calls, and Kafka with an advanced analysis engine that includes root downtime cause determination, SPC calculations, machine learning predictions, and sentiment analysis on operator notes. The product also integrates with large language models and can push analyzed data back to the plant floor with actionable insights like expected production losses.

pending_qa.q: How does transparent, flat-rate pricing affect user adoption and ROI in MES software adoption?
pending_qa.r: Transparent pricing models that are simple and flat allow companies to easily add new licenses or new users without complex per-tag or per-report licensing. This takes handcuffs off operations teams, giving them freedom to expand the platform to more desks and increase user adoption, which directly improves ROI at the bottom line.

pending_qa.q: What market shifts is the MES industry experiencing regarding IT involvement and system architecture?
pending_qa.r: The traditional level-based architecture where level two is controls, level three is MES, and level four is IT is blurring together. IT is becoming increasingly involved in the MES space and pushing down into controls like batch recipes. Additionally, manufacturing CEOs are exploring AI to improve product efficiency and profitability, though the industry is still figuring out how to effectively implement and scale AI applications.

pending_qa.q: How can AI-driven predictive insights improve proactive decision-making on the manufacturing plant floor?
pending_qa.r: Rather than after-the-fact analysis, AI can provide plant floor operators with proactive information about what to expect in production based on equipment, raw material vendors, products being manufactured, crew composition, and maintenance status. This shifts the approach from reactive to proactive, allowing operators to look out for specific issues in real time.
